stages.title: Advanced grammar
stages.hook: "Quiero que vengas" uses "vengas", not "vienes". Why does the verb change after "quiero que"?
explain: The present subjunctive is used when the main clause expresses wishes, doubt, emotion, advice or something unreal, and the subject changes: "Quiero que vengas." "Dudo que sea verdad." "Es importante que estudies." For the stem, take the yo form of the present, remove -o, and add the opposite vowel: hablar becomes hable, hables, hable; comer becomes coma, comas, coma.

Use the indicative for facts and certainty: "Creo que viene." Use the subjunctive after negated belief: "No creo que venga." Irregular subjunctives include sea (ser), vaya (ir), tenga (tener), haya (haber). Remember the weather phrase: "ojalá" plus subjunctive means I hope.
stages.mnemonic: WEIRDO: Wishes, Emotions, Impersonal expressions, Recommendations, Doubt, Ojalá.
items: it is important that you study
I do not think he comes
sentences: I do not think he is here.

gq.why: Espero que expresses hope and a different subject, so the subjunctive follows.

gq.q: What is the subjunctive of "hablar" for "tú"?
gq.why: Take hablo, remove -o, and add -es for -ar verbs.

panel.q: Why is "No creo que viene" considered non-standard?
o: Negated belief usually requires the subjunctive
panel.why: After a negated opinion, standard Spanish uses the subjunctive: no creo que venga.

panel.q: Which choice is correct? "Es verdad que ___ cansado."
panel.why: Es verdad que expresses certainty, so the indicative follows.

panel.q: Why does Spanish use the subjunctive after "quiero que"?
panel.model: The subjunctive is used for wishes and unreal or uncertain situations, especially when the subject changes.
panel.why: Mood expresses attitude.

teach.model: Use the subjunctive after wishes, doubts, emotions and advice when the subject changes, like quiero que vengas. Use the indicative for facts. Form it from the yo form and change the vowel: hablo becomes hable.

points.ask: When do I not use it?

stages.title: Complex sentence patterns
stages.hook: How can one sentence say "If I had more time, I would travel more"?
explain: Si-clauses express conditions. Real condition: "Si llueve, me quedo en casa." Unlikely or unreal present: "Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más" (imperfect subjunctive + conditional). Impossible past: "Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado" (pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect). Never use the present subjunctive or the conditional right after "si".

Relative clauses: the indicative describes a known person or thing ("Busco al hombre que vive aquí"), and the subjunctive describes an unknown or non-existent one ("Busco un hombre que viva aquí"). Para and por: para shows purpose or destination, por shows cause, exchange or the route.
stages.mnemonic: Si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional. Never "si + would".
items: If I had time, I would travel.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
I am looking for a man who lives here.
Busco un hombre que viva aquí
sentences: If I had money, I would buy it.
If she had known, she would have come.

gq.why: Si + imperfect subjunctive pairs with the conditional.

panel.q: Why is "Si sería rico, viajaría" non-standard?
o: Si is not followed by the conditional
panel.why: Standard Spanish does not use the conditional after si in an unreal condition.

panel.q: What does "Busco un libro que sea barato" suggest?
o: The speaker has no specific book in mind
The book exists and is known
panel.why: The subjunctive in the relative clause points to an unknown or hypothetical item.

panel.q: Explain the difference between "por" and "para" with two short examples.
panel.model: Por expresses cause, exchange or route (gracias por todo); para expresses purpose or destination (estudio para aprender).
panel.why: Por vs para.

teach.model: For an unreal present, use si plus the imperfect subjunctive and then the conditional. For an unreal past, use the pluperfect subjunctive and conditional perfect. Use the subjunctive after que when the thing described is unknown.

points.ask: How do I imagine the present?
How do I imagine the past?

stages.title: Extended conversations
stages.hook: How do you politely disagree with a friend in Spanish and keep the conversation friendly?
explain: Extended conversations use discourse markers: "bueno", "pues", "a ver", "o sea", "en fin". To soften an opinion: "Me parece que...", "Yo diría que...", "Tal vez...". To disagree politely: "Entiendo lo que dices, pero..." or "No estoy del todo de acuerdo."

Show you are listening with backchannels like "ajá", "claro", "¿en serio?", "ya veo". To keep the topic going, ask open questions: "¿Qué opinas?", "¿Y tú qué piensas?" Interruptions are more tolerated in many Spanish-speaking cultures than in some others, as overlapping talk can show interest.
stages.mnemonic: Pues, a ver, bueno: small words that hold a conversation together.
items: I understand what you say, but
no estoy del todo de acuerdo
sentences: I understand, but I see it differently.

gq.q: Which phrase is the most polite way to disagree?
o: No estoy del todo de acuerdo.

panel.q: Why do speakers say "a ver" before answering?
panel.why: It works as a filler marker, like "let's see".

panel.q: Why are backchannel words like "claro" and "ajá" important?
panel.model: They show that you are listening and encourage the speaker to continue.
panel.why: Backchannel cooperation.

panel.q: In Spanish-speaking cultures, overlapping speech is often seen as...
o: a sign of engagement, not necessarily rudeness
panel.why: Norms vary; overlap can signal interest.

teach.model: Use small words like bueno and pues to link your turns. Soften opinions with me parece que. Disagree gently by acknowledging the other view first. Show you listen with claro or ajá.

points.ask: How do I give an opinion?
How do I show I am listening?

stages.title: Formal and informal registers
stages.hook: You write to your best friend and to a company director. Do you use the same Spanish?
explain: Register is the level of formality. Informal Spanish uses tú (or vos), contractions of speech ("pa'" for para) and slang. Formal Spanish uses usted, polite verbs and fixed phrases: "Estimado señor López:", "Le agradecería que...", "Atentamente". Emails to friends can begin "Hola Laura," and end "Un abrazo".

The conditional and the imperfect subjunctive soften requests: "¿Podría ayudarme?", "Quisiera preguntar...". Spain also has the informal plural vosotros (habláis), while Latin America uses ustedes for both. Voseo (vos tenés) is used in Argentina, Uruguay and parts of Central America. Pronoun choice signals relationship and respect.
stages.mnemonic: Tú para amigos, usted para respeto.
sentences: Dear Mr López, I am writing to you.

gq.q: Which closing is the most formal?
gq.why: Atentamente is a standard formal closing.

gq.q: In Latin America, what is the usual plural "you" for friends?
gq.why: Latin America uses ustedes in formal and informal contexts.

panel.q: Why is "¿Podría ayudarme?" more polite than "¿Puedes ayudarme?"
o: The conditional and usted are more formal and softer
panel.why: The conditional adds distance and politeness.

panel.q: Which verb form is voseo?
panel.why: Voseo uses vos with its own verb forms.

panel.q: Why must you choose between tú and usted before writing an email?
panel.model: The pronoun shows your relationship and respect, so the wrong choice may seem rude or too distant.
panel.why: Social deixis.

teach.model: Use tú with friends and usted with people you respect. Formal letters begin with Estimado and end with Atentamente. For friends use Hola and Un abrazo. Soften requests with the conditional.

points.ask: How do I make requests softer?

stages.title: Reading articles and literature
stages.hook: "El niño que vivía en el espejo": what does a literary title promise before you read a word?
explain: Articles in Spanish-language newspapers (El País, La Nación, El Universal) use headlines with the present tense and short noun phrases. Check the lead: who, what, when, where and why. Separate facts from opinions in editorials.

Literature offers narrative voices and figurative language. Gabriel García Márquez (Colombia) is known for magical realism, where fantastic events appear in ordinary settings, as in "Cien años de soledad". Isabel Allende (Chile), Jorge Luis Borges (Argentina), Rosalía de Castro (Spain) and Pablo Neruda (Chile) are other major writers. Look for images, symbols and tone.
stages.mnemonic: Magical realism: the ordinary and the marvellous at one table.
sentences: The novel is by a Colombian author.

gq.why: It is a 1967 novel by García Márquez.

o: Fantastic events in a realistic setting
gq.why: Magical events are narrated as normal.

panel.q: Which statement in an editorial is an opinion?
o: La ley fue aprobada en marzo.
panel.why: Injusta is a judgement.

panel.q: Why do headlines often use the present tense for past events?
panel.model: It makes the news feel immediate and is brief and dramatic, which suits a headline.
panel.why: Historical present.

panel.q: Pablo Neruda was a famous poet from...
panel.why: He was Chilean and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971.

teach.model: In a news article, look for who, what, when and where. Tell fact from opinion. In literature, look at the narrator, images and tone. Magical realism mixes marvellous events with everyday life.

points.ask: What do I look for in news?
How do I tell fact from opinion?
What do I look for in stories?

stages.title: Essay and correspondence writing
stages.hook: How do you open and close a formal Spanish letter or email?
explain: An essay (ensayo) has an introduction with a thesis, body paragraphs and a conclusion. Link ideas with: en primer lugar, por otra parte, no obstante, en consecuencia, en conclusión. Support claims with evidence and examples. Keep the register formal.

Formal letters: "Estimados señores:" (Dear Sirs), "Me dirijo a ustedes para...", "Quedo a su disposición", "Atentamente". In Spanish, a colon follows the greeting, not a comma. Use accents carefully and check "sino/si no", "porque/por qué", "también/tampoco".
sentences: In conclusion, we must act now.
I am writing to ask about the course.

gq.q: Which punctuation follows the greeting in a formal Spanish letter?

gq.why: En consecuencia means as a result.

panel.q: What is the difference between "sino" and "si no"?
o: Sino means but rather; si no means if not
panel.why: No es rojo, sino azul versus Si no vienes, me voy.

panel.q: Why should an essay have a clear thesis?
panel.model: The thesis gives the main position, focuses the essay, and guides the reader through the argument.
panel.why: Argumentative structure.

panel.q: Which opening is suitable for a formal complaint?
o: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una queja formal.
panel.why: It states the purpose politely and formally.

teach.model: An essay needs a thesis, arguments with evidence and a conclusion. Use linking words like no obstante. A formal letter starts with Estimado and ends with Atentamente. Put a colon after the greeting.

points.ask: How do I write a formal letter?

stages.title: Translation fundamentals
stages.hook: Why is "Tengo 20 años" not translated as "I have 20 years" in English?
explain: Translation transfers meaning, not words. "Tengo 20 años" is "I am 20 years old." Spanish uses tener for age, hunger and thirst: "tengo hambre" (I am hungry), "tengo frío" (I am cold). English uses be.

False friends cause errors: "constipado" means having a cold, "carpeta" means folder, "sensible" means sensitive, "asistir" means to attend. Adjective position, the personal "a" ("Veo a María"), and the passive "se" ("Se habla español") need adaptation. Choose between literal and free translation depending on text type and audience.
stages.mnemonic: Translate the idea, not the dictionary.

gq.q: How is "Se habla español" best translated?
gq.why: The impersonal se often corresponds to the English passive.

panel.q: Why is "Veo a María" written with "a"?
o: Direct objects that are specific people take the personal a
panel.why: Spanish marks a specific person direct object with a.

panel.q: Why might a translator avoid word-for-word translation of an idiom?
panel.model: A literal rendering would sound unnatural or wrong, so the translator finds an equivalent expression that keeps the meaning.
panel.why: Dynamic equivalence.

panel.q: "Realizar" in Spanish most often means...
panel.why: Darse cuenta is "to realise"; realizar is to carry out or perform.

teach.model: Translate meaning, not words. Spanish uses tener for age and feelings like hunger. Watch for false friends such as constipado. Adapt impersonal se and the personal a for English.

stages.title: Regional varieties and cultural context
stages.hook: In Madrid "coger el autobús" is normal, but in parts of Latin America "coger" is avoided. Why?
explain: Spanish is spoken by hundreds of millions of native speakers in over 20 countries. Varieties differ in pronunciation (seseo vs distinción, aspiration of final s in the Caribbean, voseo in the River Plate), vocabulary (coche, carro, auto; ordenador, computadora) and grammar (vosotros in Spain, ustedes elsewhere).

In some Latin American countries the verb "coger" has a vulgar meaning, so people say "tomar" instead. Indigenous languages enrich vocabulary: from Nahuatl "chocolate", "aguacate", from Quechua "papa", "cóndor", from Taíno "huracán", "hamaca". All varieties are valid; the Real Academia Española and the Association of Spanish Language Academies record usage across countries.
stages.mnemonic: One language, many accents: say it in your own place.
sentences: I take the bus every day.

gq.q: Which language did "chocolate" come into Spanish from?
gq.why: Chocolate comes from Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs.

o: Using vos instead of or with tú
gq.why: It is common in Argentina and Central America.

panel.q: Why do Spanish-speaking countries have different words for the same thing?
o: Regional history and contact with other languages
panel.why: History, geography and indigenous languages created variety.

panel.q: Why is no variety of Spanish "more correct"?
panel.model: Each variety is valid for its community; they differ in usage, and academies record usage from all of them.
panel.why: Pluricentric language.

panel.q: Which word from Quechua is used in Spanish?
panel.why: Cóndor is from Quechua; huracán from Taíno; chocolate and tomate from Nahuatl.

teach.model: Spanish is spoken in more than twenty countries. Pronunciation, words and some grammar differ. Indigenous languages gave Spanish many words. All varieties are valid.

stages.title: Structured debates and presentations
stages.hook: How do you convince an audience in Spanish in under five minutes?
explain: A presentation (presentación) opens with a hook, introduces the topic and shows the plan: "Hoy voy a hablarles de...", "En primer lugar...", "Para terminar...". Use short sentences, pauses and eye contact. Check a formal register: "ustedes" for the audience.

In a debate (debate), state your position: "Estoy a favor de..." or "Estoy en contra de...". Give reasons: "En primer lugar, ...". Respond to others: "Entiendo su punto, sin embargo..." Avoid personal attacks and stay with the argument. Use the subjunctive to express opinions: "No creo que sea necesario."
items: Today I am going to talk to you about
sentences: Today I am going to talk about the environment.
I am in favour of the proposal.

gq.why: It states the topic to the audience.

gq.q: Which is a respectful way to counter an argument?
gq.why: It recognises the other person before disagreeing.

panel.q: "No creo que sea necesario" uses the subjunctive because...
o: it expresses doubt about the idea
panel.why: Negated belief takes the subjunctive.

panel.q: Why do speakers use signposts like "en primer lugar" and "para terminar"?
panel.model: They guide the audience through the structure, so people can follow the argument.
panel.why: Discourse organisation.

panel.q: Which fallacy is an attack on the person rather than the argument?
panel.why: An ad hominem attacks the speaker instead of answering their point.

teach.model: Open with the topic, organise your talk with signposts and close with a summary. In a debate, say whether you are for or against, give reasons and answer others politely. Use the subjunctive to give doubtful opinions.

points.ask: How do I give my position?
